summary: Provider-backed mailbox authority binds to one exact keyed PTY record and physical process generation instead of scanning the registry by subject tag.

replay.detail: No claim replay, projection rebuild, history rewrite or stored-data migration. Authority is checked against the current PTY registry at bind, repair and revalidation time.

schema.detail: No database table, column, index, trigger, claim, wire or generated-client schema change.

rules.detail: Provider mailbox authority now requires the declared exact PTY key, unchanged runtime generation, peer ancestry and a matching daemon boot identity. Missing boot identity is retryable but never authoritative; replaced or ended identity is stale.

compatibility.detail: The Smalltalk build must not be deployed while any running PTY session has a legacy registry record without daemonBootId. The deploy worker enforces the bundled check-pty-boot-identities.py preflight with no waiver.

downtime.detail: Existing live seats need a natural or authorized restart after the pty#189 runtime is deployed so their records gain daemonBootId. Restart windows remain an Operations, CoS and seat-owner decision.

manual.detail: Required order: deploy pty#189 revision 13f4d731f8898417a849de0cd655eb80dbb81e32 alone; restart live seats naturally or in an authorized window; run `PTY_ROOT=${PTY_ROOT:-$HOME/.local/state/st3/pty} pty list --json | scripts/check-pty-boot-identities.py "$PTY_ROOT"` on every host and require 0/N missing; only then deploy Smalltalk. A restarted seat whose record still lacks daemonBootId remains counted and blocks deployment.

recovery.detail: Revert the Smalltalk commit; nothing else is persisted or needs recovery.
